meta.title: Private GLP-1 Tracker — No Account, No Cloud
meta.description: Your doses, weight and symptoms stay on your phone. No sign-up, no sync, no in-app ads. Delete the app and the records on this phone go with it.

strings: No account. Your records stay on your phone.
Your injection history, weight, side effects and progress photos are stored on your device and never uploaded. A meal photo leaves the phone only if you choose to analyse it with AI calories.
A GLP-1 log is a medical record about a treatment many people do not discuss. Handing it to a service that requires an account, a login and a server is a decision, and it is usually made by default.
There is no account to make
Install it and start. Nothing to sign up for, nothing to sign in to, and nothing to delete from a server later.
Tracking works with the network off
Tracking and reminders work offline; AI meal photos and buying Premium need a connection. Uninstalling takes the records on this phone with it.
Analytics that carry no health data
Usage statistics tied to a random app ID, not your name. They record that a feature was used, never a medication, dose, weight or symptom. You can switch them off entirely.

People who are not willing to put a prescription, a weight and a symptom list behind someone else's login, and people who share a household, a phone plan or a family account and would rather this did not appear in it. Also anyone who has read what a free health app usually does with data and decided against it.

Records that only exist on one phone are lost with that phone. Dozify makes an encrypted backup file you keep yourself; there is no cloud that will quietly restore anything for you. A few things do leave the device, and the privacy policy names them: anonymous-ID usage statistics, install measurement, subscription status, and a meal photo if you choose AI analysis.
Download on the App Store
Is there an account?
No. There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to sign in to. The app opens straight into your own data.
What is collected, exactly?
Usage statistics tied to a random app ID, not your name. They record that a feature was used, never a medication, dose, weight or symptom. The privacy policy lists what is sent and what never is.
Can I get my data out?
Yes. Backup writes an encrypted, password-protected file to your device, which you keep and restore from wherever you keep it.
What happens if I delete the app?

The records on this phone go with it. Files you exported, anything you wrote to Apple Health and your own iPhone backups are separate. There is no copy on a Dozify server to come back later, which is the point and also the reason to take a backup first.
Is the data encrypted on the phone?
It is stored in the app's own database inside iOS's app sandbox, and backup files are encrypted with the password you set.
Guides, with their sources named: what GLP-1 actually is, where to inject and how to rotate, managing common side effects and how to read a health app's privacy label.
